collector.timeout_cross_check: client timeout must exceed statement+lock bounds — refused otherwise

cases.name: normal
cases.detail: one JSON document; both tables; single snapshot identity; scope check: no credentials/env/business tables in output

cases.name: lock conflict
cases.detail: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE blocker held; --lock-timeout-ms 500 refused the collector bounded (<5s, stderr LEDGER_COLLECT_ERROR lock timeout); blocker kept its lock; zero collector connections/transactions/queries survived (pg_stat_activity residue empty after excluding blocker and fixture backends); retry after release succeeded

cases.name: connection failure
cases.detail: real in-container connection refusal (PGPORT=1 forwarded to the fixture container psql); bounded <15s, LEDGER_COLLECT_ERROR

cases.name: garbage output
cases.detail: non-JSON psql output → LEDGER_COLLECT_ERROR; stdout never a plausible document

cases.name: server-side statement kill
cases.detail: statement_timeout=400ms with pg_sleep(30): server cancelled (57014 canceling statement due to statement timeout), transaction aborted, no sleeping query and no idle-in-transaction survived

cases.name: server-side lock kill
cases.detail: lock_timeout=400ms under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE: canceling statement due to lock timeout; blocker unaffected

cases.name: prod-transport job teardown
cases.detail: SCOPE-PRECISE: the client kill may leave the exec-d psql inside the container alive; the SERVER-side bounds end it — asserted against pg_stat_activity that the in-container query disappears within statement+lock bound and no aborted transaction survives (real prod channel, not a child-process return assertion)

cases.name: staging prod-channel run
cases.detail: the staged SINGLE-file collector (node --check + run, no repository context) actually executes through docker compose exec -T db against the fixture

cases.name: offline adapter exit contract
cases.detail: exit 0 = PASS, exit 1 = real BLOCK verdict, exit 2 = input refusal (MISSING_INPUT/INVALID_INPUT) before any evaluation

boundaries.note: defaults in the collector; verification exercised the same code paths with shortened values

guards.dedicated_database: test refuses any database outside ^ledger_collect_ BEFORE connecting (phoenix_erp probe refused)
guards.same_instance: the URL database must exist on the specified container AND both views must report the identical server identity before anything runs
guards.staging_prod_transport: the staged SINGLE-file collector is actually RUN through its prod channel (docker compose exec db) against the fixture in scripts/ci/ledger-collection-staging.test.mjs

shared_guard.note: single-source fixture guard (identity/dedicated namespace/same-instance ownership) — BOTH fixture suites run it before anything destructive

cases: clean fixture: rehearsal exit 0 with PREFLIGHT_RESULT=PASS and SEMANTICS=AGREE
injected fault (LEDGER_REHEARSAL_FAULT=drop-legacy-row): rehearsal exit 1, PREFLIGHT_RESULT=BLOCK with legacy_missing, EXPECTED_PREFLIGHT_VERDICT_UNMET — the gate is live, not decorative

claim_accuracy.zero_residue: RESIDUE CLAIMS ARE CHANNEL-SCOPED: the ci-channel lock-conflict residue assertion is measured (blocker/fixture backends excluded); the prod channel after a client kill relies on the SERVER-side bounds, now verified by the teardown test — a blanket zero-residue claim is not made
claim_accuracy.protection_claims: static pins (workflow YAML shape) are labelled static; dynamic proofs (corruption makes the gate fail; guards refuse probes) are labelled dynamic
